rows: ASD Temporary Mitigations for Legacy IT

Exemption granted for NDIA Participant Management System v2.1 (PMS) which cannot be migrated to a supported platform within the standard compliance timeframe due to dependencies on end-of-support middleware and planned replacement program.

PMS is scheduled for replacement under Project NOVA (FY 2026–27). Immediate decommissioning would disrupt NDIS payment processing for approximately 520,000 participants. The risk is accepted on the basis of the active replacement programme and compensating controls in place.
System hosts PMS processing NDIS participant payments; patches unavailable from vendor for core middleware component; full migration scheduled FY2026–27.

1. Enhanced network segmentation isolating PMS from external-facing systems. 2. Privileged access monitoring via PAM solution. 3. Compensating SIEM alerting rules applied. 4. Quarterly vulnerability scanning with manual review. 5. ASD legacy IT temporary mitigations applied in full.
Linked to Project NOVA ICT replacement programme. Exemption must be reviewed immediately if NOVA delivery is delayed beyond Q4 FY2026–27. Documented in NDIA Security Plan per PSPF Req 53.
Multi-Factor Authentication — Essential Eight Maturity Level Two

Exemption granted for three specialist-use workstations in the NDIA SCIF that cannot accommodate standard MFA hardware tokens due to physical security zone constraints. Restricted to named users with active NV2 clearances.

SCIF operational constraints prevent installation of standard USB/NFC MFA hardware in the secure compartment. Workstations process SECRET-classified information. Alternative smart card-based authentication (PIV) implemented as compensating control, which meets equivalent assurance.
Three SECRET workstations in NDIA SCIF; standard USB MFA tokens prohibited in zone. Named users hold NV2 clearance.

1. PIV/smart card authentication implemented (FIDO2-equivalent assurance). 2. Physical access controls to SCIF enforced (biometric + PIN). 3. Privileged activity logging and monitoring. 4. Annual review of alternative control effectiveness.
PSPF Reqs 52–53 (Contingency Planning — Alternative Mitigation Measure)
Smart card authentication meets ASD ISM guidance for equivalent assurance to hardware MFA in SECRET environments. Refer to IRAP assessor findings (Feb 2026). Annual review mandated per PSPF Req 54.
Patch Operating Systems — Essential Eight Maturity Level Two

Application for exemption submitted for NDIA HRMS (Workday) which requires vendor-managed patch deployment schedule that does not align with the NDIA 48-hour patching obligation for internet-facing systems.

Workday SaaS patches are applied by the vendor on a monthly cycle governed by the Workday SLA. NDIA does not control the patch cadence for this system. Exemption requested for the period pending renegotiation of the SLA or migration to the ASD-approved configuration.
Workday SaaS HRMS; patches managed by vendor; 48-hour patching obligation cannot be met under current SLA.

1. Contractual obligation imposed on Workday to notify NDIA of patch availability within 24 hours. 2. Enhanced monitoring of Workday environment via SIEM integration. 3. Vendor IRAP assessment reviewed quarterly.
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) — pending Accountable Authority approval

Exemption request under review. CISO has submitted risk assessment and compensating control documentation. Awaiting Accountable Authority approval. Linked to Workday contract renegotiation project (Procurement, Q3 FY2026).
